title: Japan national CPI (December 2026) + 2026 yearly average, 08:30 JST
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 2,823 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single HTML table rather than read through a summarizer. Columns are 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks'; the row parses exactly as ['December', 'January 22, 2027', 'January, 2027', 'January 29, 2027', '2026 yearly average of Japan'] — i.e. the December-2026 national CPI AND the 2026 yearly average both release on 2027-01-22, with the Tokyo January flash following on 2027-01-29. Filed estimate on three counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page's own last-update stamp is 2026-01-23, i.e. the far-forward rows have not been refreshed in ~7 months. The 08:30 JST release time is the Statistics Bureau's standing convention for the national CPI and is NOT read off this page — treat it as the weaker half of this entry
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-decision-2027-01-22 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and the reason it is tracked here: this print lands on the SAME DATE as the Bank of Japan's January 2027 MPM decision and Outlook Report (boj-decision-2027-01-22, estimate). CORRECTION, from this event's own initial research the same day: the discovering sweep recorded it as 'the only BoJ date on this calendar that shares its day with Japan's national CPI', and that is wrong. Cross-parsing boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/ against stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html, ALL SIX BoJ decisions concluding on a Friday share their date with a Statistics Bureau CPI release (2026-01-23 national Dec-2025, 2026-07-31 Tokyo July, 2026-09-18 national Aug, 2026-10-30 Tokyo Oct, 2026-12-18 national Nov, 2027-01-22 national Dec) and NONE of the four concluding on another weekday does (2026-03-19, 2026-04-28, 2026-06-16, 2027-03-18). Every one of the 30 release dates in the Bureau's table is a Tuesday or a Friday. The collision is the RULE for a Friday decision, not a January structure; the attribution warning stands, the uniqueness claim does not. Sequence within the day, on standing conventions rather than on a fetched schedule: CPI 08:30 JST, MPM decision at the meeting's conclusion around midday JST, both overnight ET, reaching the US tape as a 01-22 open. The board has the number in hand and public before it announces. The asymmetry that makes this worth a calendar row rather than a footnote: the NEXT MPM (2027-03-17/18) meets ONE DAY BEFORE the February CPI releases on 2027-03-19 (same table, row 16), so on the CPI series the January venue is the best-informed 2027 meeting and the March venue the worst. Impact is LOW, not medium: no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI, symbols is empty, and this entry's value is attribution — a 2027-01-22 Tokyo session move must be split between two Japanese events before any of it is credited to the BoJ. AND THE PRINT ITSELF IS THIN: the Tokyo December flash releases 2026-12-25 (japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25, estimate) and has landed within 0.3pp of the national core print in 78% of 103 months since 2018-01, while the '2026 yearly average' headline is the mean of twelve monthly levels of which eleven are public once the November print lands 2026-12-18 (japan-cpi-2026-12-18, estimate) — a 1.0pp December surprise moves it 0.084pp. Related dated context from the same primary table, recorded here so the next session does not re-fetch it: Japan's CPI rebased from 2020-base to 2025-base with the July-2026 national release on 2026-08-21 (Remarks column, row 9), so every Japanese CPI print the BoJ judges from 2026-08-21 onward is on the new base, and per stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/2025plan.html 'the rates of change are not recalculated with the linked index but the published values for every base period are used unmodified'.
